title: Model Diagnostics
text:
Prior Sensitivity
The half-normal(0, 0.50) prior on τ was chosen based on plausible heterogeneity in transplant outcomes. The prior places 95% of its mass below τ = 0.98, which corresponds to a range of study-level ORs spanning roughly 0.14 to 7.1 around the pooled estimate — generous for transplant outcomes.
For the PTCy coefficient, the Normal(0, 0.82) prior corresponds to 95% prior mass between OR 0.20 and 5.0, ensuring the prior does not materially constrain the posterior in any outcome.






TipAssessing Prior Influence



The Bayesian τ estimates are most informative for outcomes with k ≥ 15 (OS, CMV in C1). For sparse outcomes (BSI k=6, NRM C2 k=5), the prior provides meaningful regularisation — this is a feature, not a bug, as it prevents extreme heterogeneity estimates that would arise from fitting random-effects models to very small corpora.

This is a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of studies comparing post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) to alternative GVHD prophylaxis regimens in allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation. Two pre-specified comparisons were analysed:

title: Methods
text:
Statistical Framework

Bayesian Random-Effects Models
All models were fit using brms (v2.23.0) with the rstan backend. The general form:
\[
\text{events}_i \mid \text{trials}_i \sim \text{Binomial}(\pi_i)
\] \[
\text{logit}(\pi_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{PTCy}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{tp\_early}_i + u_{j[i]}
\] \[
u_j \sim \text{Normal}(0, \tau)
\]


Prior Specification








Parameter
Prior
Rationale




\[\beta_{\text{PTCy}}\]
Normal(0, 0.82)
Weakly informative; 95% prior mass covers OR 0.20–5.0


\[\beta_{\text{tp\_early}}\]
Normal(0, 0.50)
Timepoint adjustment; modest range


Intercept
Normal(0, 1.50)
Baseline event rate


\[\tau\]
Half-Normal(0, 0.50)
Heterogeneity; calibrated to plausible variation in transplant outcomes





Model Hierarchy

M1 (Direct effect): PTCy + timepoint adjustment + random study intercept
M2 (Steroid-adjusted): M1 + arm-level systemic steroid exposure (% receiving steroids for GVHD). Missing steroid data handled via mi() (Bayesian multiple imputation within brms) where needed.
M3 (aGVHD-adjusted, CMV only): M1 + arm-level aGVHD grade II–IV cumulative incidence



MCMC Configuration

4 chains × 4,000 iterations (1,000 warmup + 3,000 sampling) = 12,000 posterior draws
Convergence assessed via R̂ (all ≤ 1.005) and effective sample sizes (bulk ESS, tail ESS)
No divergent transitions in any fitted model



Frequentist Comparison
All Bayesian models were cross-checked with frequentist random-effects models (REML) via metafor (v5.0-1) using log-OR as the effect size. BSI in Comparison 2 (k = 3) was pooled using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect estimation.

title: Methods
text:
Arm Classification

Comparison 1
Arms were classified as PTCy if ptcy_used == "Y" and as control if the primary prophylaxis was CNI+MTX or CNI+MMF without PTCy.


Comparison 2

Primary analysis: Clean binary — PTCy-only (ptcy_used == "Y", atg_used == "N") vs ATG-only (ptcy_used == "N", atg_used == "Y")
Sensitivity analysis: PTCy+ATG combination arms reclassified as PTCy-side; mixed-ATG arms classified by PTCy co-administration; “neither” arms excluded

title: Methods
text:
GRADE Assessment
Certainty of evidence was assessed per the GRADE Handbook (Schünemann et al.) adapted for Bayesian meta-analyses of observational studies. Starting certainty: LOW. Cross-comparison coherence was considered as a potential upgrade criterion where applicable.

title: Comparison 1: PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF
text: Comparison 1 evaluates PTCy against calcineurin inhibitor–based prophylaxis (CNI+MTX or CNI+MMF) — the most common alternative platform. This comparison draws on the largest evidence base in the meta-analysis.

title: Comparison 1: PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF
text:
Overall Survival


Show code
tibble(
  M1 = post_os$b_ptcy_binary,
  M2 = post_m2_os$b_eventsn_ptcy_binary
) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Model", values_to = "log_or") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log_or, fill = Model, colour = Model)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = jama_grey) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = jama_steel)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = jama_steel)) +
  labs(x = "log-OR (PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF)", y = "Posterior density",
       title = "Overall Survival — Posterior Distributions",
       subtitle = "k = 35 studies, N = 17,661") +
  theme_jama()








Figure 1: Posterior density for the PTCy log-OR on overall survival (Comparison 1). M1 (direct effect, navy) and M2 (steroid-adjusted, grey). The vertical dashed line marks the null (log-OR = 0). Shaded regions show 95% credible intervals.





M1 (Direct effect): OR 0.77 (95% CrI 0.71–0.83), P(OR < 1) = 100%, τ = 0.59. The posterior is entirely below the null, indicating a consistent mortality reduction with PTCy.
M2 (Steroid-adjusted): Adjusting for arm-level systemic steroid exposure attenuated the OR from 0.77 to 0.83 (95% CrI 0.75–0.92), a 29% reduction in the log-OR. The residual benefit after adjustment indicates GVHD mediation does not fully explain the OS advantage.

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = jama_grey) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = jama_steel)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = jama_steel)) +
  labs(x = "log-OR (PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF)", y = "Posterior density",
       title = "Non-Relapse Mortality — Posterior Distributions",
       subtitle = "k = 15 studies, N = 2,081") +
  theme_jama()








Figure 2: Posterior density for the PTCy log-OR on non-relapse mortality. M2 adjustment abolishes the M1 benefit entirely — the hallmark of complete steroid mediation.





M1: OR 0.86 (95% CrI 0.70–1.08), P(OR < 1) = 90%. Probable but uncertain benefit.
M2: OR 1.02 (95% CrI 0.79–1.33), P(OR < 1) = 43%. Complete mediation: the NRM benefit vanishes after steroid adjustment, indicating it is entirely downstream of GVHD suppression.






ImportantComplete NRM Mediation



The M1→M2 shift (OR 0.86 → 1.02) is the single most interpretable mediation finding in the analysis. Once the steroid burden differential between arms is accounted for, there is no residual PTCy effect on non-relapse mortality.

M1: OR 1.41 (95% CrI 1.20–1.65), P(OR > 1) = 100%.
M2 (steroid-adjusted): OR 1.43 (no attenuation). M3 (aGVHD-adjusted): OR 1.52 (slight amplification). Both confirm the CMV excess operates through a steroid-independent, GVHD-independent pathway — consistent with direct impairment of CMV-specific T-cell reconstitution.

IFI (k = 8): OR 0.73 (95% CrI 0.53–1.00), P(OR < 1) = 97.5%. Probable protection, but driven by heterogeneous antifungal prophylaxis practices rather than a direct PTCy immunological effect. τ = 1.05 is dominated by a single zero-event study (Yanada 2026).

Narrative Summary
Across both comparisons, certainty does not exceed LOW — a predictable consequence of an almost entirely observational evidence base.
Cross-comparison coherence is the strongest methodological asset. OS and aGVHD show consistent effects across two fundamentally different comparators, reducing the probability that findings are artefacts of comparator-specific confounding. The mediation pattern also replicates (OS: partial; NRM: substantial/complete).
The CMV direction reversal provides moderate-certainty mechanistic evidence. Any C2 value below ~1.0 confirms a qualitative direction shift, making this finding robust to the specific C2 point estimate.
Infection outcomes remain the principal evidence gap. BSI and IFI carry VERY LOW certainty in both comparisons. Dedicated prospective studies with standardised endpoint definitions are needed.

title: Discussion
text:
The totality of findings across six pre-specified outcomes and two independent comparisons resolves into a single, internally consistent mechanistic framework built on the distinction between two immunological consequences of PTCy.


PTCy eliminates alloreactive T cells during the critical window of allorecognition, reducing acute GVHD grade II–IV by an estimated OR of 0.63 (C1) and 0.59 (C2). This propagates downstream:

NRM benefit is completely steroid-mediated in C1 (M1 OR 0.86 → M2 OR 1.02) and substantially mediated in C2 (M1 OR 0.65 → M2 OR 0.76)
OS benefit is only partially mediated (C1: 29% attenuation; C2: 35% attenuation), suggesting an additional direct contribution — most plausibly graft-versus-leukaemia preservation




The same cyclophosphamide pulse depletes the nascent CMV- and bacterial-specific T-cell repertoire. This manifests as elevated infection risk — but the direction depends on the comparator’s own depletion depth.

text:
Practical Implications
The mechanistic architecture carries direct clinical implications:








Domain
Intervention target
Rationale




CMV / BSI
T-cell reconstitution (adoptive therapy, early IS tapering)
Infection risk is GVHD-independent; steroid avoidance will not help


NRM
GVHD control and steroid minimisation
NRM benefit is fully steroid-mediated


OS
Both GVHD control + relapse prevention
Partial mediation suggests dual contribution









NoteATG Is Not the Solution



The C2 data show that ATG-based regimens carry at least as great a T-cell reconstitution liability as PTCy. The infection costs of PTCy are best understood as a general consequence of T-cell–depleting prophylaxis, not a PTCy-specific limitation.

title: Discussion
text:
Limitations

Observational evidence. All findings derive from retrospective cohort and registry studies. Residual confounding cannot be excluded despite mediation modelling.
Sparse infection data. BSI (k = 3–6) and IFI (k = 4–8) are data-poor. Dedicated prospective studies are needed.
Relapse data not analysed. The residual OS benefit (surviving steroid adjustment) is hypothesised to reflect graft-versus-leukaemia preservation, but relapse data were not extracted.
Publication bias. Formally assessed for C1 outcomes with k ≥ 10; not assessable for most C2 outcomes.
Extraction incomplete. Blocks 7–8 (99 papers) remain unextracted; the final corpus may shift some estimates.

title: Post-Transplant Cyclophosphamide Meta-Analysis
text:
Background. Post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) has become widely adopted for GVHD prophylaxis in allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation, yet comprehensive quantitative evidence synthesis across survival, GVHD, and infection outcomes — and across comparator regimens — has been lacking.
Methods. We conducted a Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of observational studies comparing PTCy to (1) CNI+MTX/MMF-based regimens (Comparison 1; k = 6–35 across outcomes) and (2) ATG-based regimens (Comparison 2; k = 5–12). Primary outcomes included overall survival (OS), non-relapse mortality (NRM), acute GVHD grade II–IV, CMV reactivation, bloodstream infection (BSI), and invasive fungal infection (IFI). Steroid-mediation models (M2) tested whether GVHD-driven steroid exposure confounded observed effects.
Results. PTCy was associated with improved OS (C1: OR 0.77 [0.71–0.83]; C2: OR 0.69 [0.61–0.78]) and reduced aGVHD (C1: OR 0.63; C2: OR 0.59) across both comparators. NRM benefit was substantially or completely mediated by steroid exposure in both comparisons. CMV reactivation showed a direction reversal: increased with PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.41 [1.20–1.65]) but decreased vs ATG (OR 0.77 [0.60–0.99]), consistent with a T-cell depletion depth hierarchy. BSI risk was elevated in both comparisons (C1: OR 2.39; C2: MH OR 2.03).
Conclusions. PTCy provides consistent survival and GVHD advantages regardless of comparator. The CMV direction reversal establishes that infection risk is determined by the relative depth of T-cell depletion, not by any intrinsic PTCy property. NRM benefit is steroid-mediated. GRADE certainty is LOW for OS and aGVHD, VERY LOW for other outcomes.

Key Findings

1. Survival and GVHD benefit. PTCy was associated with reduced overall mortality and acute GVHD in both Comparison 1 (vs CNI+MTX/MMF) and Comparison 2 (vs ATG). The effect was consistent in magnitude and direction across comparators.


2. NRM is steroid-mediated. The apparent NRM benefit was substantially or completely attenuated after adjusting for GVHD-driven steroid exposure in both comparisons, indicating that PTCy reduces NRM indirectly — through fewer GVHD episodes and less corticosteroid toxicity.


3. CMV direction reversal. PTCy increased CMV reactivation vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.41) but decreased it vs ATG (OR 0.77). This reversal confirms that CMV risk is ordered by the depth of T-cell depletion (CNI < PTCy < ATG), not by any intrinsic PTCy property.


4. BSI elevated in both comparisons. Bloodstream infection risk was approximately doubled with PTCy regardless of comparator (C1: OR 2.39; C2: MH OR 2.03), though the C2 estimate is based on only 3 studies with heterogeneous definitions.

Mechanistic Framework
The findings resolve into a unified framework built on two separable consequences of PTCy:

GVHD suppression pathway (intended): PTCy → reduced aGVHD → less steroid exposure → lower NRM → improved OS. The NRM benefit is fully steroid-mediated; the OS benefit is only partially mediated, suggesting an additional direct contribution.
T-cell lymphodepletion pathway (unintended): PTCy depletes CMV-specific and bacterial-specific T cells during engraftment. The CMV direction reversal across comparisons confirms this is a depth-of-depletion effect rather than a PTCy-specific one.

title: Risk of Bias
text:
Risk of bias (ROB) was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool (Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies – of Interventions), adapted for comparative observational studies in transplant medicine. Seven domains were evaluated:

Confounding — baseline differences between PTCy and comparator arms
Selection — participant selection into study or comparison group
Classification — misclassification of the intervention (GVHD prophylaxis)
Deviations — departures from intended interventions
Missing data — incomplete outcome data
Measurement — outcome measurement bias
Reporting — selective reporting of outcomes

Each domain was rated as Low, Moderate, Serious, or Critical risk of bias.

Key ROB Considerations by Outcome

Overall Survival







Concern
Assessment




Confounding
Moderate–Serious. PTCy arms enriched for haploidentical donors (younger, fitter recipients). M2 steroid adjustment partially addresses GVHD-mediated confounding but cannot eliminate all baseline imbalances.


Selection
Moderate. Registry-based studies reduce individual selection bias but introduce centre-level selection.


Measurement
Low. OS is an objective endpoint not subject to ascertainment bias.





CMV Reactivation







Concern
Assessment




Confounding
Serious. Donor CMV serostatus, letermovir prophylaxis, and monitoring intensity vary by arm and era.


Measurement
Moderate. CMV monitoring frequency may differ between PTCy and comparator arms (awareness bias). More intensive surveillance in PTCy arms could inflate ascertainment.


Reporting
Low. CMV reactivation is routinely reported in transplant cohorts.





BSI







Concern
Assessment




Missing data
Very serious (C1). 7 of 13 eligible studies had non-reported event counts, creating substantial attrition bias.


Classification
Moderate (C2). Outcome definitions varied (any positive culture vs ICU/fatal only).


Confounding
Serious (C2). Donor-type imbalance in the dominant study (Meyer 2025).





IFI







Concern
Assessment




Confounding
Serious. Antifungal prophylaxis regimens are heterogeneous and non-randomly distributed. PTCy centres disproportionately use prolonged mold-active azole prophylaxis.


Measurement
Moderate. IFI diagnosis requires invasive procedures (bronchoscopy/biopsy); investigation intensity may differ between arms.

title: Risk of Bias
text:
Impact on Interpretation
Risk of bias is a consistent limitation across all outcomes, reflecting the almost exclusively observational evidence base. The mediation models (M2, M3) partially address confounding by adjusting for GVHD-driven steroid exposure, but residual confounding from baseline characteristics (age, disease risk, donor type, conditioning intensity) cannot be excluded.
The most robust findings are those where:

The effect survives covariate adjustment (OS, CMV in C1)
The direction is consistent across comparators with different confounding structures (OS, aGVHD)
Plausible bias would oppose rather than inflate the observed effect (aGVHD)
